source.title: Non-convergence of stochastic gradient descent in the training of deep neural networks
source.authors: Patrick Cheridito; Arnulf Jentzen; Florian Rossmannek

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper gives theoretical results showing that SGD can fail to converge for ReLU networks under specified depth, width, and initialization-count conditions. It does not test the benchmark classification-error settings in the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The results concern theoretical bounds on expected clipped true risk for an abstract supervised-learning setup, not CIFAR benchmarks or classification training error. No cited prior-work results are recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study proves non-convergence bounds for fully connected ReLU networks using expected true absolute-error risk. It does not test any listed version's specified behavior and setting. Its depth, width, and initialization results do not establish the benchmark training-error, teacher-student, initialization-comparison, stability, or normalization claims.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly correct. More precisely, the authors prove failure of expected true-risk convergence along specified highly depth-imbalanced ReLU architecture sequences when random restarts grow too slowly. This is not a claim that all increasingly deep and wide networks fail, or that the SGD parameter trajectories fail to converge.
record.recipe_differences: The paper provides a mathematical analysis of an abstract SGD procedure and proves risk lower bounds; it does not reproduce the benchmark training recipes described in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The non-convergence result depends on the depth-to-width imbalance and the number of random initializations relative to architecture size.

fits_no_version.finding: Independent random initialization can place a fully connected ReLU network in an inactive region that SGD cannot escape. For specified depth-width and restart-count conditions, this yields a true-risk lower bound, positive for a nonconstant target.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For some ReLU architecture sequences whose depth grows sufficiently rapidly relative to width, too few independent random restarts prevent expected true approximation risk from tending to zero, regardless of training duration.

record.problems: The results are theoretical bounds in an abstract supervised-learning setup. They do not provide empirical benchmark measurements, training classification error, or numerical architecture settings for an applied run.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying results were left out.

untested.parts: CIFAR-10/100 training classification error in convolutional networks, including random labels and the effects of size, early stopping, and regularization.
Spurious-minimum frequency in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and the benefit of one or two extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks, identity-shortcut comparisons, and the specified initialization exceptions.
Activation-matched initialization comparisons, signal and gradient preservation, learning speed, and trainable depth under Gaussian versus orthogonal initialization.
Learning rates relative to stability thresholds, transient loss increases, curvature changes, and edge-of-stability dynamics.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and tolerated learning rates, and comparisons with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Theoretical results can test a version, but these results concern a different architecture and outcome from those specified here. Neither row warrants a verdict on V1–V6.

versions.untested_parts: Does not measure training classification error on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, or compare model sizes, early stopping, and regularized recipes.
Does not study two-layer teacher-student networks, spurious local minima, or student width relative to teacher width.
Does not compare plain and residual networks or measure training error by depth; the theoretical depth-width imbalance result is not a test of the version's shortcut comparison.
Does not compare initialization schemes for training speed or trainable depth.
Does not test learning rates relative to a stability limit, loss spikes, curvature, or sharpness.
Does not compare batch normalization with no normalization or test Fixup.
